name: Excelsior Renewable Energy Management Company LP (Excelsior Energy Capital)
headquarters: Excelsior, Minnesota (21960 Minnetonka Blvd, Suite 210; the Minneapolis suburb the firm is named for), with offices in Portland, Oregon and New York
employees: 25 (Form ADV annual amendment, 30 March 2026); the team page lists 24 named people
summary:
BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: Excelsior Energy Capital is a Minnesota fund manager that owns and operates US wind, solar and battery assets through two closed-end funds — Fund I (USD 504 million, 2021, fully deployed, now in harvest) and Fund II (just over USD 1 billion, April 2025, anchored by the Development Bank of Japan) — and, since 2023, develops and builds its own solar-plus-storage pipeline through the wholly-owned platform Lydian Energy; its relevance to this corpus is that it reserved 9.7 GWh of US-made batteries in 2024 (2.2 GWh of Fluence Gridstack Pro, 7.5 GWh of LG Energy Solution Vertech) against a Lydian pipeline that carries roughly 4.4 GW of solar and storage, and no source yet names the project that has received either.

BACKGROUND. Founded in 2017 by four former TerraForm Power executives (Chris Moakley, Anne Marie Denman, Alex Ellis, Ryan Fegley). The SEC-registered adviser is Excelsior Renewable Energy Management Company LP (CRD 289890) with USD 1,505,418,687 of regulatory assets under management across two pooled vehicles and 47% non-US clients, per the March 2026 Form ADV. Fund I closed at USD 504 million in January 2021 (Form D/A: USD 503,787,879 sold to 27 investors, first sale 8 September 2017) and was deployed across 16 investments and 1.95 GW, per the Fund II release; Fund II closed at 'just over $1 billion' against a USD 750 million target on 8 April 2025, over 50% deployed across 15 investments and 2.25 GW. Flagship asset: Faraday Solar in Utah County, 685.3 MWdc / 525 MWac, financed at USD 1.3 billion in November 2023 and in commercial operation from 30 September 2025 under PacifiCorp's 20-year Schedule 34 contract with Meta as the buyer of the energy and attributes. Lydian Energy, launched April 2024 with 1.75 GW across nine Texas and New Mexico projects, has since financed three Texas batteries (550 MW / 1.1 GWh, USD 233 million, July 2025) and a USD 689 million tranche (Faraday BESS Phase 1 150 MW / 733 MWh, AC Ranch 1, Yellow Viking; February 2026), and bought Hanwha Renewables' ~1.5 GW Atlas North portfolio in April 2026. Fund I exits: a 38-project distributed portfolio to BlackRock (December 2023) and an 830 MW operating wind and solar portfolio to Enel for about USD 1 billion (signed February 2026, closing expected in the third quarter of 2026; seller entity Excelsior Renewable Energy Intermediate Fund I LP, per trade press).
ecosystemRole: A buyer of batteries rather than a builder of them: Excelsior is the counterparty in two of the largest US-made storage supply frameworks on the corpus — Fluence's 2.2 GWh Gridstack Pro agreement (July 2024) and LG Energy Solution Vertech's 7.5 GWh agreement (December 2024) — both signed to capture the Inflation Reduction Act domestic-content bonus. Through Lydian it owns merchant batteries in ERCOT (with CATL cells) and contracted storage in Utah and CAISO, and through Faraday it sells solar to Meta via PacifiCorp. Its 2025–2026 Stella Power and CleanAmps alliances point the platform at firm power for data centres, so far without a named site or offtaker.

productsAndServices.name: Closed-end renewable infrastructure funds (Fund I and Fund II)
productsAndServices.description: Excelsior raises and manages closed-end private equity funds that buy, finance, own and operate US wind, solar and battery projects. Fund I (Excelsior Renewable Energy Investment Fund I LP) closed at USD 504 million in January 2021 against a USD 500 million target; Fund II (Excelsior Renewable Energy Investment Fund II LP, with Feeder Funds II-A and II-B) closed at 'just over $1 billion' against USD 750 million on 8 April 2025, anchored by the Development Bank of Japan.
highlights: Fund I: USD 503,787,879 sold to 27 investors (Form D/A, 29 January 2021); 17 investors from six countries per the close release; 'fully deployed across 16 investments totaling 1.95 GW' per the Fund II release; placement agents Probitas, Consilium, Trinity, MMX Global.

Fund II: 'just over $1 billion' vs USD 750 million target; first close USD 502 million (March 2023); anchor Development Bank of Japan Inc.; 'Over 50% deployed across 15 investments' and '2.25 GW' at close; SEC Form Ds through May 2024 show USD 234.05 million (main LP, 9 investors), USD 246.16 million (Feeder II-A, 24 investors) and USD 200 million (Feeder II-B, 2 investors) sold — a floor, not the final size.
Form ADV (30 March 2026): regulatory AUM USD 1,505,418,687 across 2 pooled vehicles; 25 employees; 47% non-US clients; minimum commitment USD 10 million; related-person ownership 5%.

Investor types per the releases: pension plans, insurance companies, fund-of-funds, asset managers, leasing companies, endowments, family offices and financial institutions from the US, Japan, Europe, Australia and the Middle East.

Fund I is in harvest: 38-project distributed portfolio sold to BlackRock's Evergreen Infrastructure Partners Fund (December 2023) and an 830 MW wind and solar portfolio to Enel Green Power North America for about USD 1 billion (signed February 2026; seller named as Excelsior Renewable Energy Intermediate Fund I LP by Pulse 2.0).
productsAndServices.positioning: A middle-market owner-operator rather than a mega-fund: Fund I and Fund II together are roughly USD 1.5 billion of equity against Brookfield, Blackstone or BlackRock GIP vehicles an order of magnitude larger. Excelsior's stated edge is 'speed, flexibility, and certainty of execution' and an in-house portfolio-operations team; its 2017 mandate was 'to own and operate renewable investments with contracted returns'.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct LP fundraising with placement agents (Probitas Partners, The Trinity Group, Consilium Capital, DBJ Securities); Sidley Austin as fund counsel.
targetSegments: Institutional limited partners — pension plans, insurers, fund-of-funds, endowments, family offices (US, Japan, Europe, Australia, Middle East)
productsAndServices.roadmap: No Fund III has been announced on any first-party channel as of September 2026; every 2025–2026 release still says 'two active funds'. A third-party page claiming a USD 1.8 billion Fund III is uncorroborated and is not relied on here.

productsAndServices.name: Owned operating portfolio — utility-scale solar, wind and distributed solar
productsAndServices.description: The assets the funds own and operate, headed by Faraday Solar (Utah County, 685.3 MWdc / 525 MWac, COD 30 September 2025) and including Prairie Breeze II and III wind (109 MW, Nebraska, acquired from Invenergy 2019–2020), Skyhawk Solar (Tennessee, TVA/Google), El Centro (25 MWdc, California), the Syncarpha and Nokomis distributed portfolios, and the Investments-page entries the firm lists by state (Arizona, California, Colorado, Massachusetts, Minnesota, Nebraska, New Mexico, New York, Tennessee, Texas, Utah, Vermont, Washington).
highlights: Faraday Solar: USD 1.3 billion financing closed November 2023 — USD 400 million tax equity from U.S. Bancorp Impact Finance via a solar production tax credit partnership, USD 460 million senior loan, USD 300 million tax-exempt bank loan, USD 250 million ancillary facilities; MUFG and Nord/LB coordinating lead arrangers; '1.2 million solar panels'; EPC Energy Project Solutions and RES; offtake 'PacifiCorp's 20-year power purchase agreement via Rocky Mountain Power's Schedule 34 green energy tariff' with Meta 'purchasing energy and environmental attributes'.

Prairie Breeze II & III: 109 MW combined, 90.1% sponsor equity interest acquired from Invenergy; offtakers Lincoln Electric System (Moody's AA) and City of Grand Island (AA-); Nord/LB back-leverage, Bank of America Merrill Lynch tax equity.
Skyhawk Solar (Obion County, Tennessee): 100 MW with Origis Energy under TVA's Green Invest programme for Google's data centres; groundbreaking July 2022; Wanzek EPC.

Homepage counters: '33+' portfolio investments and '6.4 GWs' of capacity; the Investments page lists Excelsior NDS1 (520 MW, Arizona), White Creek (204.7 MW, Washington) and Mustang Hills plus Mustang Hills BESS (150 MW each, California) with no release describing them — collection gap.

Exits: 38 distributed solar and solar-plus-storage projects (89 MWdc, six states) to BlackRock, KeyBanc lead sell-side advisor, closed December 2023; 830 MW operating wind and solar to Enel for about USD 1 billion (EUR 850 million), enterprise value about USD 1.3 billion, ~2.1 TWh a year, EBITDA about USD 145 million per Enerdatics — conditions include antitrust, FERC and foreign-direct-investment review.
productsAndServices.positioning: Contracted, investment-grade offtake is the pattern on the owned book — PacifiCorp/Meta at Faraday, AA-rated municipal buyers at Prairie Breeze, TVA at Skyhawk, Xcel community-solar tariffs in Minnesota. The Enel sale at roughly 8x EV/EBITDA (Enerdatics' arithmetic) is the first public read on what that book is worth.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Long-term PPAs and utility tariffs to utilities, municipal buyers and hyperscalers via utility green tariffs; assets sold at exit to strategic and infrastructure buyers (BlackRock, Enel).
targetSegments: Investor-owned utilities and their green-tariff customers (PacifiCorp / Meta)
Municipal and public power buyers (Lincoln Electric System, Grand Island, TVA / Google)
Community-solar subscribers under state programmes (Xcel Energy, Minnesota)
productsAndServices.roadmap: Enel acquisition expected to close in the third quarter of 2026 subject to antitrust, FERC and FDI review; Faraday BESS Phase 1 (150 MW / 733 MWh) is under construction at the Faraday site under the February 2026 Lydian financing.

productsAndServices.name: Lydian Energy — wholly-owned development, construction and ownership platform
productsAndServices.description: Lydian Energy LLC (Washington, DC; CEO Emre Ersenkal) was co-founded with Excelsior in 2023, launched publicly on 9 April 2024 with 1.75 GW across nine Texas and New Mexico projects, and is described by trade press as wholly owned by Fund II. It develops, finances, builds and will operate utility-scale solar and BESS: three Texas merchant batteries (Pintail 200 MW, Crane 200 MW, Headcamp 150 MW; USD 233 million from ING and KeyBank, July 2025), a USD 689 million tranche for Faraday BESS Phase 1, AC Ranch 1 and Yellow Viking (CIBC and MUFG, February 2026), and the ~1.5 GW Atlas North acquisition from Hanwha Renewables (April 2026). Its site lists '5.1 GW of solar & storage projects; 17 projects across 6 states'.
highlights: Texas BESS (July 2025): Pintail (San Patricio County) 200 MW / 400 MWh, Crane (Crane County) 200 MW / 400 MWh, Headcamp (Pecos County) 150 MW / 300 MWh per the release (Energy-Storage.news reports 391 / 521 / 521 MWh — the two figures are not reconciled by any source); ING about USD 139 million for Pintail and Crane, KeyBank USD 94 million for Headcamp; tax credit bridge with Fund II co-investment; CATL batteries per Energy-Storage.news; 'ERCOT merchant market but may explore offtake contracts'; release COD target Q4 2025, ERCOT queue record for Headcamp shows July 2026 and Lydian's site still lists all three 'In Construction'.

February 2026 USD 689 million (CIBC, MUFG): construction-to-term loan, tax credit bridge, co-investment bridge, letter-of-credit facility — Faraday BESS Phase 1 150 MW / 733 MWh (Utah, 'long-term investment-grade PPA' with PacifiCorp), AC Ranch 1 75 MWac / 100 MWdc (New Mexico, busbar PPA), Yellow Viking 170 MWac / 210 MWdc (Texas, Oncor territory, 100 MW under PPA).

Atlas North (April 2026): four late-stage projects from Hanwha Renewables — 1,000+ MW solar plus 450 MW / 1,800 MWh BESS — with a 500 kV gen-tie to CAISO via Cielo Azul Switchyard and Ten West Link; 'vast majority' contracted to California load-serving entities; 'Lydian's largest investment to date'; price undisclosed.
Pipeline restated across releases: 1.75 GW / 9 projects (April 2024) → 4.7 GW / 20 projects (July 2025) → 4.4 GW / 18 projects (February 2026) → 5.1 GW / 17 projects on the site after Atlas North.

Governance: Excelsior's releases name Anne Marie Denman as Chair of Lydian's board (April 2024 launch) and Chris Moakley as 'Chair of the Board at Lydian Energy' in the February and April 2026 releases — the two releases differ and no source explains the change.
productsAndServices.positioning: Lydian is how an owner-operator captures development margin without becoming a greenfield originator: its projects are acquired late-stage (Atlas North from Hanwha, the Texas batteries developed under Fund II) and taken through financing and construction in-house. Peers on this corpus that own ERCOT merchant batteries are Spearmint Energy, Hunt Energy Network and Jupiter Power; Lydian's differentiator is the parent's reserved US-made supply and PTC/ITC financing stack.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Project-level construction-to-term debt (ING, KeyBank, CIBC, MUFG), tax credit bridge loans and Fund II equity co-investment; merchant ERCOT revenue on the Texas batteries, PPAs elsewhere.
targetSegments: ERCOT merchant energy and ancillary-service markets (Pintail, Crane, Headcamp)
Investment-grade utility offtakers (PacifiCorp at Faraday BESS)
productsAndServices.roadmap: Pintail, Crane and Headcamp COD slipped from the released Q4 2025 target (Headcamp queue record: July 2026); Faraday BESS Phase 1, AC Ranch 1 and Yellow Viking in construction under the February 2026 financing; Atlas North build-out timing undisclosed.

productsAndServices.name: Battery and module supply frameworks — Fluence 2.2 GWh, LG Energy Solution Vertech 7.5 GWh, Heliene 2 GW
productsAndServices.description: Multi-year supply agreements signed in 2024 to lock domestic-content-qualifying equipment for the Excelsior/Lydian pipeline: Fluence Gridstack Pro, 2.2 GWh, deliveries from 2025, cells 'primarily manufactured in Tennessee' (Fluence's site identifies AESC's Tennessee plant and a 305 Ah LFP cell) and modules made by Fluence in Utah (30 July 2024); LG Energy Solution Vertech, 7.5 GWh of 'fully integrated' containerized LFP long-cell systems with AEROS software, first delivery April 2026 (19 December 2024); Heliene, 2 GW of PV modules mostly from Mountain Iron, Minnesota (10 April 2024).
highlights: Fluence: 'Gridstack Pro is one of the first energy storage solutions expected to qualify as domestic content under the Inflation Reduction Act'; Utility Dive: 'five to 10 project sites' including ERCOT and CAISO, storage-only and hybrid; IRA 10% bonus credit. Neither release names a recipient project; Excelsior appears in no Fluence SEC filing or in the Q3 FY2026 call (EDGAR full-text search, zero hits).

LG Energy Solution Vertech: 7.5 GWh, 'multi-year', 'All projects will meet domestic content requirements'; KED Global estimates the deal at KRW 1.8 trillion (about USD 1.24 billion) and names the JF2 AC Link system — Korean press estimate, not in LG's release; no plant, end year or project is named by any source.
Heliene: 2 GW over multiple years; 'A majority of the PV modules supplied by Heliene would be produced in the United States'; PV Tech ties the volume to Faraday and Lydian.

Combined battery reservations of 9.7 GWh against a disclosed Lydian pipeline of about 4.4 GW at the time of the LG deal; Lydian's CEO said the two deals 'do not have an impact on Lydian's three projects', which use CATL cells with LG as 'secondary supplier' per Energy-Storage.news.
Proximal Energy (15 October 2024): multiyear AI asset-management agreement covering 'Excelsior's pipeline includes 2 GWh of storage projects'.
productsAndServices.positioning: Among covered buyers, Excelsior's 7.5 GWh LG framework sits alongside DTE (6 GWh), Terra-Gen (8 GWh) and Qcells (5 GWh) in LG Energy Solution's US pipeline, and its 2.2 GWh Fluence order predates Fluence's first domestically manufactured delivery (September 2025). The reservations are the firm's answer to FEOC and tariff exposure on Chinese cells — while its first three operating-stage batteries still carry CATL.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct framework/reservation agreements between the fund manager and the OEM, drawn down project by project.
targetSegments: Excelsior- and Lydian-owned storage and hybrid projects in ERCOT, CAISO and the West
productsAndServices.roadmap: LG first delivery slated April 2026 (not confirmed delivered by any source); Fluence deliveries 'beginning in 2025' (no delivery to Excelsior confirmed by any source as of September 2026).

productsAndServices.name: Firm power and data-centre initiatives — Stella Power alliance and CleanAmps collaboration
productsAndServices.description: Two 2025–2026 alliances that point the platform at large-load customers: Stella Power Company (8 September 2025) — hybrid plants integrating natural gas generation with renewables and BESS for 'Data centers, utilities, energy-intensive businesses', deliverable in '18 months or less' with 'minimum guaranteed carbon-free energy targets'; and CleanAmps Holdings (2 July 2026) — an expanded 'advisory, system engineering, and joint infrastructure development' collaboration for a 'U.S.-owned Digital Infrastructure Platform' citing '3 GWh of Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) integration projects completed' and '10+ GWh of strategic battery procurement initiatives, including FEOC-compliant and Section 45X-eligible battery storage solutions'.
highlights: Stella Power: no MW, site or customer disclosed; Denman: 'The Stella team have developed a solution that complements and differentiates what Excelsior can provide to the marketplace.'

CleanAmps: 'more than three years of successful collaboration'; platform described as 'modular data center architecture, firm power integration, high-availability controls, and industrial-grade cybersecurity'; Fegley: 'the next wave of infrastructure investment will increasingly focus on the intersection of power and compute.' No MW, site or signed offtake disclosed.
The only hyperscaler-linked revenue on the record is indirect: Faraday's energy and attributes go to Meta via PacifiCorp Schedule 34, and Skyhawk serves Google via TVA Green Invest.
productsAndServices.positioning: Excelsior is entering the firm-power-for-data-centres lane late and through partners; covered developers already there (Intersect Power's energy parks, Fermi-class campuses) hold sites and interconnection. Excelsior's assets are the reserved batteries, the tax-credit stack and a PacifiCorp/Meta precedent.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Advisory and joint-development alliances; no product is sold yet.
targetSegments: Data centres and other large energy users seeking 24/7 or firm low-carbon power
productsAndServices.roadmap: No dated deliverable: neither release names a site, an offtaker or a first project.

relationships.note: Multiyear 2.2 GWh agreement for US-made Gridstack Pro systems (Tennessee cells, Utah modules) with deliveries beginning in 2025, signed 30 July 2024.
relationships.context:
Fluence's release: 'Excelsior will deploy Fluence's Gridstack Pro product line' with 'battery cells primarily manufactured in Tennessee and battery modules manufactured by Fluence in Utah'; 'one of the first energy storage solutions expected to qualify as domestic content under the Inflation Reduction Act'. Utility Dive adds five to 10 project sites across ERCOT and CAISO, storage-only and hybrid. Denman and Frantz quoted for Excelsior, John Zahurancik for Fluence.

What the record does not show: which project receives the systems, and whether any have been delivered — Fluence's September 2025 first-domestic-delivery release names no customer, Excelsior appears in no Fluence SEC filing (EDGAR full-text search, zero hits) and was not mentioned on Fluence's Q3 FY2026 call. Lydian's CEO said the Fluence and LG deals 'do not have an impact on Lydian's three projects'. The agreement is company-confirmed by both sides; its execution is not yet visible.

relationships.via: LG Energy Solution Vertech integrated LFP long-cell systems (AEROS software)
relationships.note: Multiyear 7.5 GWh agreement with LG Energy Solution Vertech for fully integrated, US-made LFP storage systems, first delivery slated for April 2026, announced 19 December 2024.
relationships.context:
LG's release (Westborough, Massachusetts): '7.5 GWhs of fully integrated lithium-ion energy storage projects'; 'containerized lithium-ion battery solutions with LFP long cells' with AEROS software, integration and lifecycle services; 'First delivery slated for April 2026'; 'All projects will meet domestic content requirements and will be delivered to the U.S.' KED Global values the deal at KRW 1.8 trillion (about USD 1.24 billion) and names the JF2 AC Link system — a Korean press estimate, not in the release.

The corpus's LG Energy Solution dossier lists the deal in LG's US pipeline alongside DTE (6 GWh), Terra-Gen (8 GWh) and Qcells (5 GWh) and dates cells to Holland, Michigan for 2028–2030; no fetched source names the plant, an end year or the recipient projects, and LG is described by Energy-Storage.news as a 'secondary supplier' to Lydian, whose first three Texas batteries use CATL. Whether the April 2026 first delivery occurred is not confirmed by any source.

relationships.note: Lydian's first three ERCOT batteries — Pintail, Crane and Headcamp — use CATL battery systems, per Energy-Storage.news; the Lydian release names no supplier.
relationships.context: Energy-Storage.news (10 July 2025) reported the USD 233 million financing 'for three Texas BESS provided by CATL' and quoted Lydian's CEO that the Fluence and LG agreements 'do not have an impact on Lydian's three projects'; its February 2026 coverage calls LG a 'secondary supplier' with CATL primary. The attribution is trade-press-sourced — Lydian's own release lists lenders and MW/MWh but no battery supplier — so it is recorded as reported, with the outlet named. It matters because Excelsior's stated procurement strategy is US-made, domestic-content supply, while its first operating-stage batteries carry Chinese cells with FEOC optics.

relationships.note: Meta buys Faraday Solar's energy and environmental attributes under PacifiCorp's 20-year power purchase agreement through Rocky Mountain Power's Schedule 34 green energy tariff.
relationships.context: Excelsior's COD release (30 October 2025): Faraday 'commenced commercial operations September 30, 2025', with Meta 'purchasing energy and environmental attributes under PacifiCorp's 20-year power purchase agreement via Rocky Mountain Power's Schedule 34 green energy tariff'. The contract counterparty is the utility; Meta is the tariff customer behind it — the indirect hyperscaler structure this corpus's utility dossiers describe. Faraday BESS Phase 1 (150 MW / 733 MWh) is being added under a PacifiCorp PPA per Lydian's February 2026 financing.

policyExposure.exposure: Excelsior's 2024 supply frameworks were built to capture the Inflation Reduction Act domestic-content bonus: Fluence's Gridstack Pro is 'one of the first energy storage solutions expected to qualify as domestic content under the Inflation Reduction Act' (Utility Dive: a 10% bonus tax credit), LG Energy Solution Vertech committed that 'All projects will meet domestic content requirements', and Heliene modules are majority US-made. Faraday Solar was financed with USD 400 million of tax equity 'via solar production tax credit partnership', and Lydian's 2026 financing carries a 'Tax Credit Bridge Loan'.
policyExposure.mitigation: Reserved US-made supply (2.2 GWh Fluence, 7.5 GWh LG, 2 GW Heliene) and the CleanAmps collaboration's '10+ GWh of strategic battery procurement initiatives, including FEOC-compliant and Section 45X-eligible battery storage solutions'.

policyExposure.exposure: Lydian's first three operating-stage batteries (Pintail, Crane, Headcamp) use CATL systems per Energy-Storage.news, which flags the foreign-entity-of-concern context; the same outlet describes LG as a secondary supplier. The firm's own July 2026 release names 'FEOC-compliant and Section 45X-eligible battery storage solutions' as the procurement target. No source quantifies the exposure or reports a project affected.
policyExposure.mitigation: Company statement (CleanAmps release, 2 July 2026): procurement initiatives 'including FEOC-compliant and Section 45X-eligible battery storage solutions'.

financials.commentary: Collection gap: no revenue, EBITDA, fee income or fund returns are disclosed. The size figures that exist are the Form ADV regulatory AUM (USD 1.505 billion), fund closes (USD 504 million; just over USD 1 billion), project-level financings (USD 1.3 billion Faraday; USD 233 million and USD 689 million Lydian) and the Enel sale price (about USD 1 billion, trade-press-sourced).

strategyRead: 1. **(High confidence)** We assess that Excelsior is an owner-operator with a captive late-stage development arm, not a greenfield developer — and that the `developer` category rests on Lydian alone. Basis: the founders' own mandate language ('own and operate renewable investments with contracted returns'), the 2019–2022 partner structures in which Unico, Nokomis, Regis and Renewable America developed while Excelsior 'acquires projects upon construction start', and Lydian's growth by acquisition (Atlas North's 'four late-stage projects' from Hanwha). No source shows Excelsior or Lydian originating sites or filing its own interconnection requests.

2. **(High confidence)** We assess that the 9.7 GWh of reserved US-made batteries is a procurement option sized to the pipeline rather than a delivery schedule, and that its draw-down is unverified. Basis: neither the Fluence nor the LG release names a project; Lydian's first three batteries use CATL cells and its CEO said the two frameworks 'do not have an impact on Lydian's three projects'; Fluence has never named Excelsior in an SEC filing or earnings call; no delivery to an Excelsior site is reported as of September 2026. The July 2026 CleanAmps release restates the volume as '10+ GWh of strategic battery procurement initiatives'.

3. **(Moderate confidence)** We assess that the contracted book is worth roughly 8x EBITDA to a strategic buyer and that Fund I will return most of its equity through the Enel sale. Basis: about USD 1 billion consideration and about USD 1.3 billion enterprise value for 830 MW with about USD 145 million EBITDA (Enerdatics' arithmetic on Enel's figures) against a USD 504 million fund; closing is still subject to antitrust, FERC and FDI review, and Excelsior itself has issued no release on the sale.

4. **(Moderate confidence)** We assess that Lydian's merchant ERCOT batteries are behind schedule and that the platform is rotating toward contracted storage. Basis: the July 2025 release targeted Q4 2025 in-service for Pintail, Crane and Headcamp; the ERCOT queue record for Headcamp shows July 2026 and Lydian's site lists all three 'In Construction' in September 2026; the February 2026 tranche is entirely PPA-backed and Atlas North is 'vast majority' contracted to California load-serving entities. The MWh figures for the Texas batteries differ between the release and Energy-Storage.news and no source reconciles them.

5. **(Low confidence)** We assess that the data-centre and firm-power pivot (Stella Power, CleanAmps) is positioning without a project. Basis: neither release names a site, MW or offtaker; the only hyperscaler revenue on the record runs through utilities (Meta via PacifiCorp Schedule 34 at Faraday; Google via TVA at Skyhawk). A named large-load offtaker or a gas-hybrid site would move this judgment.

Collection gap: no fund returns, fee terms or Form ADV Part 2 brochure; no first-party statement on the Enel sale; the Investments page lists assets (NDS1 520 MW Arizona, White Creek 204.7 MW Washington, Mustang Hills and Mustang Hills BESS 150 MW each) that no release describes; the Portland office address differs between the homepage (6600 SW 92nd Ave) and the contact page (9900 SW 92nd Ave); one 7 April 2026 Business Wire item could not be identified. Premise check against the coverage-plan row: 'Fluence's 2.2 GWh US-made supply customer' holds, but the agreement dates from July 2024 (not December) and December 2024 is the separate 7.5 GWh LG deal; 'investor · developer' holds only through Lydian.

INDICATORS TO WATCH — *Q3 2026 — Enel closing:* completion confirms the ~8x read and Fund I's harvest; a lapse would signal FERC or FDI friction. *2026 — first named Fluence or LG delivery to an Excelsior/Lydian site:* would convert Judgment 2 from option to execution; another year without one confirms it. *2026 — Pintail, Crane, Headcamp COD:* energisation dates in ERCOT records versus the Q4 2025 target. *2027 — a Fund III first close or Form D:* would end the 'two active funds' boilerplate. *Any Stella or CleanAmps site announcement with a data-centre offtaker:* the trigger for Judgment 5.
